newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's Tabaqueira sale could be in 96 - minister.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Tabaqueira sale could be in 96 - minister.

text.p: The privatisation of a 65 percent stake in Portuguese cigarette manufacturer Tabaqueira could take place in 1996, Economy Minister Augusto Mateus said.
"It could happen in 1996," Mateus told reporters after the swearing-in ceremony of the Competition Council.
Last week Mateus referred the privatisation of Tabaqueira to the Competition Council, which has 30 days to give an opinion on the likely impact of the sale on the local market.
Mateus will have a further 15 days to consider the bids.
"There is no reason why the deadlines will not be met," Mateus said. "The Competition Council may give its opinion quickly, and I may take a quick decision."
He added: "We have a privatisation coming which may strengthen an already dominant position in the market. The impact on the level of concentration has to be authorised or not, as the case may be."

The Economy Ministry, which is responsible for the state's industrial holdings, had decided to seek the opinion of the Competition Council because whoever won the bidding would dominate the local tobacco market.
Tabaqueira accounts for 70 percent of Portuguese cigarette sales.
The privatisation of Tabaqueira is due to take place this year, according to the government's privatisation calendar.
Government officials had said previously that they hoped the privatisation would be wrapped up in early November.

The candidates to buy Tabaqueira are the U.S. group Philip Morris, in partnership with Portugal's Jorge de Mello group; state-owned Spanish tobacco company Tabacalera, allied to Madeira company Empresa Madeirense de Tabacos; and French group Seita.
